summary: Baileys fork with char-code-obfuscated hardcoded network host in message-send path
details: alipclutch-baileys is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library. lib/Socket/messages-send.js contains a hardcoded network destination reconstructed from a String.fromCharCode(...) decimal-array at lines 425 and 436, which decodes to https://fiora.nixel.my.id/. The destination is not a documented Baileys endpoint and is embedded inside the message-sending code path. The obfuscation of the host (assembling the URL from a char-code array rather than a plain string) is characteristic of covert exfiltration or covert command channels wired into an ostensibly benign WhatsApp client library; consumers using this fork to send messages route traffic and message-related data through an author-controlled endpoint they did not configure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
